minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 12, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:00 p.m., on April 12, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 8, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN # 78452136 and
  #784521-41. Agency Negotiator: Keith Rattay, Dennis Wilberg. Negotiating Party:
  Casa Loma Condominium Association, Platinum Group Management, Inc. Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms Related to Trail Segment (Creekside.)

CS2. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
City Council Minutes  1  April 12, 2016
   Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered two closed session items.
For CS1, the Council gave direction to staff to commence discussions but nothing was approved
and any final actions will be addressed in public. For agenda item CS2, the Council gave direction
to staff but there was no final reportable action at this time.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO)-Municipal Services Review

  Carolyn Emery, Orange County LAFCO Executive Officer, provided a brief update on
  south Orange County governance.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Pastor Mike Maiolo, M.V.: announced that the National Day of Prayer is on May 5, 2016. He
thanked the City Council for allowing his and other churches to hold an event and this year, it will
be held at the Potocki Center. He encouraged residents to come together in unity to pray.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that getting control of police and fire authority costs seems to
be at the forefront of the recall efforts in Lake Forest. He said that what happens in the City of
Lake Forest could have a ripple effect in Mission Viejo and he further discussed police contract
costs.

Jim Farris, M.V.: expressed concern with the services and personnel working at the Mission Viejo
recreation center which is run by the YMCA.

Vanessa Christian, M.V.: expressed concern with the vote that will be taken at the Orange County
Mosquito and Vector Control Board Meeting of April 21, 2016, regarding the spraying of a
chemical called Duet. She stated that she does not support aerial spraying of pesticides and she
wants her group to be represented at the vote of the Board on April 21.

City Council Minutes  2  April 12, 2016
 Stephen Masek, M.V.: expressed concern with the report drafted by Kosmont on the Village
Center.

Randy Smith, Friends of the Mission Viejo Library Board Member, M.V.: shared that the 100
volunteers of the Friends of the Library have contributed $2.2 million towards library expenditures.
Mr. Smith called the Council's attention to National Library Week which the Friends will celebrate
with a fundraiser at CPK restaurant and a sale at the bookstore. Also, Waste Management will
give a donation to the library for all residential recycling collected during the month of April

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 22, 2016, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated March 11, 2016 in the Amount of $551,990.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Bocce Ball Courts at Oso Viejo Community Park- (CIP 324) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $8,696.64, thirty-
  five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
City Council Minutes  3  April 12, 2016
 10. Budapest Avenue Storm Drain Installation (CIP 836)

  Approved Change Order 1 to the contract with Metra Construction, Inc., in the amount of
  $2,771.00.

12. Purchase of Library Self-Check Systems

  (1) Approved issuance of purchase order to SirsiDynix in the amount of $38,964.20 for
  purchase and installation of 3M self-check kiosks, and (2) adopted Resolution 16-11 for
  Transfer of $39,000 from Library Fund 632-201-8400 to IT Fund 233-201-8400.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15. Amended City Investment Policy for FY 2015-16

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt
  Resolution 16-13 Approving the Amended City Investment Policy for FY 2015-16.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16. Adopt a City based IRC Section 115 Irrevocable Retirement Funding Trust Fund;
  Authorize Management of the Trust and Funds and Authorize a Transfer of Reserves
  in an Amount Not to Exceed Three Million Dollars Sum into the Established Trust

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve
  the creation, funding and management of an IRC Section 115 Irrevocable Retirement
  Funding Trust Fund per the attached Trust Documents.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17. Proposed Funding Agreement Between the City of Mission Viejo and the Santa
  Margarita Water District to Provide Financial Assistance for the Construction of the
  Lake Mission Viejo Advanced Purified Water Treatment Facility
City Council Minutes  4  April 12, 2016
   City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the proposed funding agreement for the Lake Mission
  Viejo Advanced Purified Water Treatment Facility: Kevin Pennington, President of the Lake
  Mission Viejo Association Board of Directors; Charley Wilson, President of Santa Margarita
  Water District; and Robert Breton, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the Water
  Treatment Facility Funding and Recycled Water Purchase Agreement (A16-07) subject to
  any final technical/non-substantial changes made by the City Attorney. The contract will be
  amended to add a new section E to the Finding and Recitals as follows: “The City Council
  reasonably finds, on the totality of the record, including the oral and written testimony for
  this and related action items that this Agreement will promote a direct, valid and substantial
  public purpose which is within the City’s authorized mission and power and which will
  directly assist the City in accomplishing its authorized public responsibilities, despite
  according incidental benefit to individuals or entities receiving derivative benefits.”

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

NEW BUSINESS

13. Resolution Supporting Housing Futures Initiative Sponsored by BIA-OC; Orange
  County Business Council and Orange County Association of Realtors

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following made comments in support of the proposed resolution: Steven LaMotte,
  Building Industry Association, Irvine; Rita Tayenaka, M.V.; and Jocelin Jimenez, Orange
  County Business Council, Irvine.

  The following presented comments in opposition to the proposed resolution: Stephen Masek,
  M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution
  16-12 In Support of the Housing Futures Initiative Developed by The Building Industry
  Association - Orange County Chapter, The County Business Council, and The Orange
  County Association of Realtors.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  5  April 12, 2016
   AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Raths and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:01 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:13 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

14. Economic Development Ad Hoc Committee - Award of Consultant Contract to SWA
  Group to Prepare a Civic Core Area Vision Plan

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed contract for a civic core vision plan: Larry
  Gilbert, M.V. and Stephen Masek, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  and authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with SWA Group (A16-06) in an
  amount not to exceed $199,932.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register Dated March 18, 2016 in the Amount of $1,929,510.54

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she has noticed, for a number of years, that the
  City has been paying over $5,000 a year for a storage unit rental for the Marine Adoption
  Committee. She asked what is being stored and said that in her opinion, the money is being
  thrown away on storage and could be better spent on things the Marines need.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg responded that the Adoption Committee collects items that
  are to be transported to Camp Pendleton and they use the storage unit to store the items until
  they can be taken to the base.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  6  April 12, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Check Register Dated March 25, 2016 in the Amount of $371,936.53

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment made to “Express Yourself” for reserved
  parking signs for the Potocki Center.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that he doesn’t have that information available and staff
  will get back to the Council with an answer.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Raths, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Alicia Parkway to Alarcon - (CIP
  225) - Notice of Completion.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that the original budget for the project was $600,000 and the
  final project came in at $426,000. She asked if the terms of the contract were met.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the
  contractor performed the work on a tight time frame and did a great job.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) certify the
  completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the City
  Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record Notice of
  Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful Performance and Payment
  Bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days respectively, after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4)
  authorize the payment of the final retention of $19,479.17, thirty-five (35) days after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  April 12, 2016
 8.  Eldorado Park Playground Renovations - (CIP 305)

  Council Member Schlicht remind Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith
  Rattay that they had a conversation about playgrounds that are mostly tot lots and she said
  that she is hoping to get consensus to have the Community Services Commission look at
  opportunities to have more age appropriate playgrounds at some of the City parks.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve
  the plans and specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the Eldorado Park
  Playground Renovations - (CIP 305).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Pavion Park Restroom Construction - (CIP 304)

  Council Member Schlicht asked how ACT 1 came down $54,000 on their bid.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that he doesn't
  know but staff checked the contractor’s references and they heard great reviews so there is
  no indication that they will not do a good job.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to award contract to
  Act 1 Construction, Inc. (A16-04) for the construction of Pavion Park Restroom in an amount
  not to exceed $327,668.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11. Traffic Signal Maintenance-Battery Back-up Systems

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her continued concern with the visibility of traffic
  signals along Muirlands and she stated that staff really needs to look at the height of the trees.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay suggested that they go out
  and drive on Muirlands together so Council Member Schlicht can show him her concerns.

City Council Minutes  8  April 12, 2016
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to award contract in the
  amount of $96,125.00 to Siemens, Inc., (A16-05) to provide and install seven new traffic
  signal battery back-up systems.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

18. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA)

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed the threat of the City of Irvine leaving the Orange
  County Fire Authority and the union's efforts to recoup monies from the member cities.

  Council Member Sachs presented the report and asked the City Manager to appropriate
  $5,000 towards the $135,000 campaign on drowning prevention.

20. PACE Program Ad Hoc Committee - PACE Information Packet for Residents

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she would like to postpone this matter until the
  City has heard back from realtors on the proposed information packet. Mayor Pro Tem
  Bucknum said that the realtors have already provided input.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he has been against PACE programs and the City's
  involvement from day one.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum (no second) to approve the use of the information
  packet for resident education regarding PACE programs with the use of Alternate A for the
  cover letter.

  SUBSTITUTE motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member
  Schlicht, to table this matter.

  On roll call, said substitute motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  9  April 12, 2016
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Raths

22. Laguna Niguel Gateway Specific Plan - Development Update Including Traffic and
  Emergency Response

  Planning Manager Larry Longenecker provided an update on traffic impacts and infrastructure
  improvements relative to the Gateway Plan in Laguna Niguel.

Council Member Raths thanked Lt. NewMyer and the Orange County Sheriff's Department for
arresting a resident who was getting into mailboxes and stealing checks. He also congratulated
fire department personnel for their quick response to the fire at a sushi restaurant in town. Council
Member Raths announced that he represented the City at a Veterans Spring Summit at the Richard
Nixon library and it was a fantastic event. He asked staff if the La Paz widening project is going
to start soon and City Manager Wilberg explained that the delay is due to Federal government
funding. Council Member Raths announced that he is spearheading the Rotary Club's annual
fundraiser which will be a Texas Hold 'Em tournament on June 11, 2016. Lastly, he asked the
City Attorney to describe the policy that the Council recently adopted on campaign signage.

Council Member Sachs

Addressing Council Member Raths' concern with OCFA response times, Council Member Sachs
explained that units are dispatched based on which unit is available at the time. He outlined data
that staff supplied on workmen's comp claims and payments through the California JPIA. He
asked that staff investigate the cost of private insurance for workmen's comp.

Council Member Schlicht

23. Consideration of Subscription to CustomScoop Media Monitoring Service

  Council Member Schlicht asked that this item be postponed.

Council Member Schlicht thanked Council Member Sachs for the town hall meeting he hosted on
sober living homes. She assured the public that the entire Council is on board with finding some
way to regulate these group homes. Council Member Schlicht gave the City Clerk an advance
copy of an agenda report that she plans to place on the next agenda regarding term limits with a
lifetime ban. She stated that she doesn't mean to be abrasive or argumentative with her colleagues
but her number one job is to be a voice of the public. In closing, she quoted Dwight D. Eisenhower:
City Council Minutes  10  April 12, 2016
 "Any time you deny any citizen the full exercise of his constitutional rights, we are weakening our
own claim to them."

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that she attended an infrastructure tour of Rancho Mission
Viejo to look at the work that is being done to try and mitigate traffic issues. She commended the
County for their efforts and she encouraged residents to stay informed of what is going on around
them because some cities take on the task of widening roads to help with traffic and others
don't. She outlined her attendance at a casino night event to benefit Relay for Life and she
announced that the Mission Viejo Library will be hosting the monthly Chamber of Commerce
Mixer on April 21, at 5:30 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum also announced upcoming events
including an Earth Day event on April 23, Up in the Air on April 16 and Arts Alive on April 30
and May 1. She further announced that the Rotary Prayer breakfast is on May 5 and she
encouraged residents to carpool if they attend the National Day of Prayer event at the Potocki
Center. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed her appearance on The City Square radio show where
she and Mayor Ury discussed water issues and other things going on in Mission Viejo, including
the animal shelter's proposal to provide services to the cities of Laguna Hills and Rancho Santa
Margarita. In closing, she asked that the Mayor adjourn the meeting in memory of Chapman
University’s economic forecaster, Dr. Adibi.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury agreed that Dr. Adibi did some excellent economic forecasting and he was able to
explain trends and calculations to policy makers in terms that they could understand.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:55 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Dr. Esmael Adibi, to Tuesday, April 26, 2016, at
5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 26, 2016

City Council Minutes  11  April 12, 2016
